purpose: Empirical noise floor of the ArcFace cosine metric under identity-preserving nuisance.
interpretation: Cosine similarity is not a probability and there is no calibrated identity threshold. These perturbations never change identity, so every measured change is metric sensitivity, not identity drift. T is an envelope for the nuisance families in the frozen grid only; families not modelled (expression, true 3D pose, age) can push a same-identity score lower, which makes T a lower bound and 'inside envelope' verdicts permissive.
claim_under_test: In the historical pilot, Maya's assigned ArcFace similarity fell after the second pass in all four multi-pass scenes.

settings.multi_face_rule: sort by bbox[0]; if several faces remain, use the largest bbox area, then the leftmost
settings.resolution_note: Downscale sizes are short sides of the warped image. In the embed-only regime the aligned crop is already 112 px, so the 224/160/112 levels cannot downscale and are recorded as no-ops (cosine 1.0).
settings.pose_model: planar perspective warp of the image plane about the landmark centroid of the face; no 3D render, no self-occlusion

realistic_tier.rule: identity preserved for a human observer under ordinary photographic variation
realistic_tier.excluded_from_T: pose beyond 20 deg, gamma outside 0.7-1.4, gain outside 0.8-1.25, shading above 0.5, downscale below 160 px, blur above sigma 1, JPEG below q50, occlusion above 10%, sunglass and mask bands
realistic_tier.justification: Each included level matches an ordinary photographic or rendering variation. Excluded levels remove the cues the embedder uses (eyes, mouth, fine detail) rather than re-rendering the same face, so folding them into T would inflate the floor until no real change could be detected.

baseline_verification.note: Harness embeddings against evaluation/results/scores.json. Differences are float32 storage in the frozen file, not a pipeline change.
